summary: Valve announced the Steam Deck OLED, a mid-cycle refresh of the Steam Deck with a 7.4-inch 90Hz HDR OLED screen, a more efficient 6nm APU, and a 50Whr battery. Engadget reviewed it and measured a 62 percent playtime increase in Hades. Valve is also restructuring the lineup and prices, with the LCD model reduced to a 256GB entry version, and hinted at future handhelds and controller prototypes.
one_line: Valve launches the Steam Deck OLED on November 16 with a better screen, a more efficient chip and a bigger battery, and reshuffles pricing.
key_facts: The Steam Deck OLED has a 7.4-inch OLED screen versus the original's 7-inch 800p LCD, with the same resolution but a refresh rate of up to 90Hz instead of 60Hz.
The OLED display is HDR, covers 110 percent of the P3 color space and has a peak brightness of 1,000 nits, compared with around 400 nits on the old model.

The new APU is a die-shrunk 6nm version of the original 7nm chip; Valve chose efficiency over performance, and max CPU and GPU frequencies match the LCD model so developers have a single performance target.
The battery is 25 percent larger at 50Whr versus 40Whr; Valve claims a 30-50 percent longevity increase and a battery life of "three to 12 hours".
Engadget measured a 62 percent playtime increase when playing Hades on the OLED model versus its 18-month-old original Steam Deck.

Other upgrades include Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3, a slightly larger fan, thumbsticks 1mm taller, sharper touch pad haptics, and a power supply with a 2.5m cable that charges from 20 to 80 percent in "as little as 45 minutes".
The new lineup is 256GB LCD at $399, 512GB OLED at $549 and 1TB OLED at $649, plus a Limited Edition 1TB model with a translucent shell and custom carry case at $679.

The 64GB LCD model drops from $399 to $349 and the 512GB LCD drops from $649 to $499; both will be discontinued once inventory sells through, though Valve will keep supporting LCD models with software updates.
Anti-glare etched glass is available only on the premium 1TB OLED model, which also gets an improved carry case.
Valve's Greg Coomer called the OLED model "the definitive version of the Steam Deck".
Valve engineer Pierre-Loup Griffais said the company has "plans for successive generations of handhelds" as long as interest remains high.
Coomer said Valve is still working internally on "a bunch of controllers and prototypes", with no announcements on a Steam Machine or updated Steam Controller.
The Steam Deck OLED can be ordered on November 16th at 1PM ET, with shipping starting as orders come in.
